messages:
incident-bot: :warning: Pager P0 - smart-routing unexpected fallback. Telemetry shows an uptick in user-reported low-quality outputs coincident with a routing policy change. Top symptom: short, truncated answers and hallucinated facts for compliance-sensitive tenants. Link: https://alerts.redwood.internal/alerts/9091

alex (oncall-sre): Ack. Taking ownership. Summon ml + platform.

maria (ml-eng): On it. Seeing reproducible low-quality samples on our regression harness. Variant 'xk-lite-quant' is getting traffic for requests that previously went to 'xk-large-stable'. Many cases where the prompt expects detailed citations are now empty or invented.

tom (support): Customer impact: 4 enterprise accounts (contracts, billing, compliance) reporting failures. Zendesk threads: 12210,12211,12212. One customer automated contract review pipeline flagged 9 mismatches.

raj (platform): I rolled out the 'adaptive-cost' matcher earlier in the region eu-central-1 ~50m ago (PR #4321). It adds a cost tier signal to route cheaper quantized variants for non-interactive routes. Need to verify matcher priority order; logs show rule evaluation changed.

alex (oncall-sre): Short-term mitigation: block 'xk-lite-quant' from production traffic in eu-central-1 and set a tenant-pin for affected accounts. I can apply an ACL rule. Maria, will this stop the regressions?

maria (ml-eng): Yes, that should stop the regressions for those tenants. Note: fallback will increase token cost and some latency; communicate that to customers.

raj (platform): Applying ACL now. Command:

```
# block quant variant in eu-central
rwctl variants block --region eu-central-1 --variant xk-lite-quant --who=raj
```

deploy-bot: acl change started by raj (change id: acl-2026-03-15-11)

alex (oncall-sre): ACL applied. Verified traffic: quant variant usage in eu-central down from 32% -> 0% for production routes.

maria (ml-eng): Re-running regression set for affected tenants. Initial pass: quality metrics returned to baseline on pinned traffic.

tom (support): I've notified CSMs for impacted tenants and posted a status note: "We detected degraded outputs due to routing change; we've temporarily blocked the cheaper model variant and are investigating root cause."

alex (oncall-sre): Root cause hypothesis: PR #4321 unintentionally bumped 'cost' to higher precedence during matcher compilation, so tenant pins were treated as lower-priority soft hints. That allowed cost-driven fallbacks to override explicit pins.

maria (ml-eng): Confirmed in policy logs: matcher order for several routes shows 'cost' evaluated before 'tenant_pin'. We'll need a fix in the policy compiler to preserve pin precedence.

raj (platform): I will prepare a policy compiler patch to restore explicit pin precedence and add a regression test. Meanwhile, I'll revert the matcher change for eu-central and add a rollout guard. Plan: revert for region only, then patch globally.

raj (platform): Revert command:

```
# revert adaptive-cost matcher in eu-central
rwctl policy revert --region eu-central-1 --change 4321 --who=raj
```

deploy-bot: policy revert started by raj (change id: rv-2026-03-15-12)

alex (oncall-sre): Revert applied. Traffic looks stable, pinned variants in place.

maria (ml-eng): Adding integration eval to ensure any future matcher PRs cannot change pin semantics. Will add tests in evaluation harness and in policy CI that simulate pinned tenants + cost signals. ETA: PR tomorrow.

tom (support): Customer update sent. One customer replied asking for timeline on permanent fix, please include expected timelines in postmortem.

alex (oncall-sre): Handoff to sasha: summary - adaptive-cost matcher rollout in eu-central caused cost preference to override tenant pins, resulting in quantized low-cost variants serving sensitive requests. Mitigations: blocked variant in region, tenant pins applied for affected customers, region-level matcher revert. Actions: confirm follow-ups, monitor error/quality dashboards for 12h, coordinate with customer success on replies.

sasha (oncall-next): Acked. I'll run the 12h checks and keep an eye on any reappearance. Please tag me on the postmortem.

raj (platform): Post-deploy plan: patch policy compiler, add CI smoke to validate pin precedence, and add rollout gating that enforces a 'pin-compatibility' test for matcher changes. Also add a circuit-breaker: if quality signals drop > X% in 5m, auto-disable cost routing.

maria (ml-eng): I'll produce a small corpus of failing prompts and attach it to the postmortem so we can track regressions. Also recommending stricter stage gating for quant variants in regions with enterprise tenants.

alex (oncall-sre): Incident timeline: PR 4321 deployed ~1871234200, anomalies first seen ~1871234300, pager fired ~1871234567, mitigation (ACL + revert) ~1871234580. Estimated exposure ~25m. Impact: 4 enterprise customers, multiple automated failures, severity P0 -> mitigated to P1. Postmortem owners: maria + raj + alex. Deliverables: timeline, root cause, code patches, CI tests, customer comms draft.

deploy-bot: acl-2026-03-15-11 succeeded. rv-2026-03-15-12 succeeded.

incident-bot: Incident mitigated. Follow-ups required: postmortem, CI tests, customer follow-up.

tom (support): I'll collate ticket list and attach examples to the postmortem.

sasha (oncall-next): Thanks all. I'll monitor and escalate if needed. :thumbsup:
